run.checkpoint_rule: each checkpoint is the banked statline THROUGH a quarter boundary, read off the play rows' own quarter column: pre = no play at all, q1/q2/q3 = through that quarter, final = THROUGH THE END OF REGULATION, and ot = through the last play of the game. A game that never went to overtime has no ot checkpoint, because it would be the same checkpoint as final written twice
run.need_rule: the need is the WHOLE-NUMBER threshold a counted market asks for (a 4.5-reception line needs 5 catches) and the line itself on a measured one, which is `sweat.need_for` — the same rule the sweat board prints. `needs` at a checkpoint is that need minus the banked value, floored at zero; it is never negative and it is never a chance
run.state_rule: a checkpoint's state is ONLY what arithmetic knows: `cashed` when the banked value has reached the need (`cashed_at` names the checkpoint it first crossed at), `lost` at the LAST checkpoint when it never did, and `open` everywhere else. No state on this file was inferred from a chance, because no chance exists for this week
run.statline_rule: a player's statline carries a record for every tracked market he has a captured week-1 line for, PLUS every tracked market he banked a non-zero value of, so the line reads as a statline and not as a list of bets. A record with no captured line carries `line`, `need`, `odds_american`, `book`, `cashed_at` and every checkpoint `needs` and `state` as null: there is a stat but there is no bet, and a bet is never invented to fill the slot
run.line_of_record: per (player, market): each book's LATEST capture at each line is the row of record; the MAIN LINE is the line the most books quote (one book, one vote), ties breaking on the LOWER line; and the price carried on the row is the OVER price from the book whose capture at that line is the MOST RECENT, ties breaking on the book name. It is a price a named book actually posted — never a median, never a best-of, never a shopped number
run.player_id_rule: nflverse's receiver_player_id / rusher_player_id / passer_player_id are GSIS ids and our player_id IS the gsis id (db.models.Player, and ingest.settle writes gsis_id = player_id), so id_crosswalk.gsis_id -> player_id is consulted first and the identity is the fallback — the same read edge.secondary and metrics.opportunity make when they alias a pbp id straight to player_id. No mapping is invented here
run.chance_absent_reason: no engine distribution existed for week 1 (the ESPN-plug week, D-074 amendment E) and no live model exists yet (L4)

the book's spelling of the player's name is not on id_crosswalk.book_name_variants and the row carried no player_id, so the quote resolves to no player of ours
the line's game has no pbp-nflverse row banked for this slate, so there is no play-by-play to replay
the live capture stored no week-1 main line for this tracked market at all, so no bet of it can appear on the board
